scene-root.name: Week 7 KP07 DenseNet, later architectures and a review of the chapter (guided version)

scene-u01.name: Week 7 KP07 DenseNet, later architectures and a review of the chapter (guided version)

p01-hook-title.name: p01-hook-title
p01-hook-title.text: What if we connect the outputs of 'all' earlier layers?

p01-hook-ctx.name: p01-hook-ctx
p01-hook-ctx.text: The residual block of KP06 connects the output of earlier layers to later ones by 'addition', linking only the input and output of one block. DenseNet takes the shortcut to the extreme.

p01-hook-res-t.name: p01-hook-res-t
p01-hook-res-t.text: ResNet: the shortcut links only 'the input of this block' to 'the output of this block', by addition.

p01-hook-dn-t.name: p01-hook-dn-t
p01-hook-dn-t.text: DenseNet: in a dense block every layer is connected to all later layers, by concatenation.

p01-hook-q-t.name: p01-hook-q-t
p01-hook-q-t.text:
This unit answers four questions:
1. How many connections are in a dense block?
2. How do addition and concatenation differ in their effect on channels?
3. Can the channel count get out of control? (growth rate and transition layer)
4. What came after ResNet? What does the whole Week 7 add up to?

p02-dense-title.name: p02-dense-title
p02-dense-title.text: How many connections are in a dense block?

p02-dense-ctx.name: p02-dense-ctx
p02-dense-ctx.text: A standard network of $l$ layers connects only adjacent layers (about $l$ weight matrices). Layer $\ell$ of DenseNet receives $\ell$ inputs $x_0,\dots,x_{\ell-1}$ ([Added] counting the block input $x_0$).

p02-dense-c1-t.name: p02-dense-c1-t
p02-dense-c1-t.text: Adjacent: $4$ connections (green) = the standard network's wiring.

p02-dense-mis-t.name: p02-dense-mis-t
p02-dense-mis-t.text: Common error: thinking DenseNet has an unusually large number of layers. The point is many connections: every layer gets the outputs of all earlier layers directly.

p03-add-concat-title.name: p03-add-concat-title
p03-add-concat-title.text: Addition and concatenation: how do they differ for channels?

p03-add-concat-ctx.name: p03-add-concat-ctx
p03-add-concat-ctx.text: The difference between ResNet and DenseNet is how earlier outputs are used later.

p03-add-concat-add-t.name: p03-add-concat-add-t
p03-add-concat-add-t.text:
Formula (11): $x_\ell=\mathcal{F}_\ell(x_{\ell-1})+x_{\ell-1}$
the two sides must have equal shapes, and after adding the channel count is unchanged.

p03-add-concat-cat-t.name: p03-add-concat-cat-t
p03-add-concat-cat-t.text:
Formula (12): $x_\ell=\mathcal{F}_\ell\bigl([x_0,\dots,x_{\ell-1}]\bigr)$
all earlier outputs are joined along the channels and fed into $\mathcal{F}_\ell$: the channel count grows more and more.

p03-add-concat-cl.name: p03-add-concat-cl
p03-add-concat-cl.text: Concatenation: channel count grows layer by layer (example: $k_0=16,\ k=12$)

p03-add-concat-fl-t.name: p03-add-concat-fl-t
p03-add-concat-fl-t.text: In a dense block $\mathcal{F}_\ell$ is usually batch normalization + $3\times3$ convolution + ReLU (original order: BN, ReLU, convolution). Within one dense block the feature-map sides must be equal for concatenation, so pooling sits in the transition layer [Added]. Here $\ell$ counts one layer operation; the $\ell$ of formula (11) in KP06 corresponds to one residual block (two convolution layers).

p04-growth-title.name: p04-growth-title
p04-growth-title.text: Concatenation raises the channels all the way — how to control it? The growth rate

p04-growth-ctx.name: p04-growth-ctx
p04-growth-ctx.text: Each convolution layer produces only a few new feature maps; their number is the growth rate $k$. A block input has $k_0$ channels and layer $\ell$ sees $k_0+k(\ell-1)$ input maps. Example: $k_0=16$, $k=12$, six layers ([Added]).

p04-growth-wsum-t.name: p04-growth-wsum-t
p04-growth-wsum-t.text: The six layers add up to $29,808$ weights ($9\times\text{input}\times12$).

p04-growth-good-t.name: p04-growth-good-t
p04-growth-good-t.text: Benefits: many shortcuts, good gradients, features can be reused, and every layer is narrow.

p05-practice-a-title.name: p05-practice-a-title
p05-practice-a-title.text: Your turn: connections, number of input maps and weights

p05-practice-a-q1-t.name: p05-practice-a-q1-t
p05-practice-a-q1-t.text: A dense block has $l=5$ layers. How many connections does it have? And a standard network?

p05-practice-a-q2-t.name: p05-practice-a-q2-t
p05-practice-a-q2-t.text: $k_0=24$, $k=12$: how many input maps does layer $4$ see? How many channels at the end of the block after six layers?

p05-practice-a-q3-t.name: p05-practice-a-q3-t
p05-practice-a-q3-t.text: $k_0=16$, $k=12$: how many weights does the $3\times3$ convolution of layer $3$ have?

p05-practice-a-a1-t.name: p05-practice-a-a1-t
p05-practice-a-a1-t.text: $l(l+1)/2=5\times6/2=15$; the standard network has $5$. That is $1+2+3+4+5=15$.

p05-practice-a-a2-t.name: p05-practice-a-a2-t
p05-practice-a-a2-t.text: Layer 4: $24+12\times3=60$; after six layers: $24+12\times6=96$. Each layer adds $12$ more maps.

p05-practice-a-a3-t.name: p05-practice-a-a3-t
p05-practice-a-a3-t.text: The input of layer 3 is $16+12\times2=40$; weights $3\times3\times40\times12=4,320$.

p06-transition-title.name: p06-transition-title
p06-transition-title.text: Between blocks: what does the transition layer do?

p06-transition-ctx.name: p06-transition-ctx
p06-transition-ctx.text: When several dense blocks are chained, a transition layer between blocks controls complexity: batch normalization, $1\times1$ convolution, $2\times2$ average pooling.

p06-transition-r8-t.name: p06-transition-r8-t
p06-transition-r8-t.text: Channels halved and side halved: the total number of feature-map values drops to $1/8$.

p06-transition-cls-t.name: p06-transition-cls-t
p06-transition-cls-t.text: The last stage is average pooling and a fully connected layer with softmax for classification. Common error: thinking concatenation makes the channel count run away — the growth rate $k$ is small and the transition layer compresses, so the channel count can be controlled.

p07-compound-title.name: p07-compound-title
p07-compound-title.text: EfficientNet: enlarge depth, width and resolution together

p07-compound-ctx.name: p07-compound-ctx
p07-compound-ctx.text: Before, often only one of them was enlarged; EfficientNet (2019) enlarges them together in fixed proportion. The source gives no numbers; the constants below come from the original paper ([Added]).

p07-compound-fm-t.name: p07-compound-fm-t
p07-compound-fm-t.text: Depth $\times\alpha^{\phi}$, width $\times\beta^{\phi}$, resolution $\times\gamma^{\phi}$, with $\alpha\beta^{2}\gamma^{2}\approx2$ (computation is roughly proportional to it).

p07-compound-cx-t.name: p07-compound-cx-t
p07-compound-cx-t.text: ConvNeXt (2022) modernizes the CNN design and competes with the Transformer: in the age of attention models, the CNN has not gone out of date.

p08-practice-b-title.name: p08-practice-b-title
p08-practice-b-title.text: Your turn: transition layer, compound scaling, addition versus concatenation

p08-practice-b-q1-t.name: p08-practice-b-q1-t
p08-practice-b-q1-t.text: A transition layer compresses $88$ channels into $44$. How many weights does the $1\times1$ convolution have? How large is $56\times56$ after average pooling?

p08-practice-b-q2-t.name: p08-practice-b-q2-t
p08-practice-b-q2-t.text: $\alpha=1.2,\ \beta=1.1,\ \gamma=1.15$, $\phi=2$: by how many times are depth, width and resolution enlarged? About how many times the computation?

p08-practice-b-q3-t.name: p08-practice-b-q3-t
p08-practice-b-q3-t.text: ResNet and DenseNet both use earlier outputs later, one by addition and one by concatenation. What is the effect on the channel count of each?

p08-practice-b-a1-t.name: p08-practice-b-a1-t
p08-practice-b-a1-t.text: $88\times44=3,872$; $2\times2$ average pooling with stride $2$: $56\to28$. Channels and side both halve, and the total drops to $1/8$.

p08-practice-b-a2-t.name: p08-practice-b-a2-t
p08-practice-b-a2-t.text: Depth $1.2^{2}=1.44$, width $1.1^{2}=1.21$, resolution $1.15^{2}=1.3225$ times; computation about $1.9203^{2}=3.69$ times.

p08-practice-b-a3-t.name: p08-practice-b-a3-t
p08-practice-b-a3-t.text: Addition: equal shapes, and the channel count is unchanged after adding. Concatenation: channels stack up more and more, so DenseNet needs a small growth rate and transition layers to control the channels.

p09-review-title.name: p09-review-title
p09-review-title.text: Review of Week 7: every architecture answers the question left by the previous one

p09-review-ctx.name: p09-review-ctx
p09-review-ctx.text: Each row: what this unit added and what question it left to the next.

p09-review-rt02.name: p09-review-rt02
p09-review-rt02.text: Random starts break symmetry; He and Xavier keep the signal from vanishing or exploding

p09-review-rt12.name: p09-review-rt12
p09-review-rt12.text: Deep CNN, ReLU, LRN, overlapping pooling, GPUs; 60,954,656 weights, 96.2% in the fully connected layers

p09-review-rt22.name: p09-review-rt22
p09-review-rt22.text: Stacks of small 3×3 kernels; VGG-16 has 138,344,128 weights

p09-review-rt33.name: p09-review-rt33
p09-review-rt33.text: What if the output must be per pixel?

p09-review-rt42.name: p09-review-rt42
p09-review-rt42.text: Contraction, expansion and skip connections; 31,023,808 weights

p09-review-rt53.name: p09-review-rt53
p09-review-rt53.text: What if all earlier layers are connected?

p09-review-rt62.name: p09-review-rt62
p09-review-rt62.text: Concatenation, feature reuse; compound scaling; modernized CNNs

p09-review-nt-t.name: p09-review-nt-t
p09-review-nt-t.text: The numbers of weights are computed in the earlier units of this week from the kernel sizes and layer settings (biases not counted); U-Net has 1 input channel and 2 output classes, AlexNet and VGG-16 have 1000 classes, so the three should not be compared directly; the source gives no whole-network parameter counts for Inception, ResNet or DenseNet, so none are listed.

p10-conclusion-title.name: p10-conclusion-title
p10-conclusion-title.text: Conclusions of this chapter (convolutional neural networks)

p10-conclusion-ctx.name: p10-conclusion-ctx
p10-conclusion-ctx.text: Organized from the source, three points.

p10-conclusion-c1-t.name: p10-conclusion-c1-t
p10-conclusion-c1-t.text: CNNs specialize in grid data (images). A layer's three stages are convolution → detector (activation) → pooling, instead of flattening the image into a fully connected layer (Week 6).

p10-conclusion-c2-t.name: p10-conclusion-c2-t
p10-conclusion-c2-t.text: Starting from LeNet and AlexNet, VGG, Inception, ResNet and DenseNet each raise the stakes in depth, efficiency and feature reuse.

p10-conclusion-c3-t.name: p10-conclusion-c3-t
p10-conclusion-c3-t.text: The Transformer has become mainstream in many fields, but CNNs remain key in computer vision, medical imaging and edge devices, and are the foundation for understanding modern deep learning.

p11-misconceptions-title.name: p11-misconceptions-title
p11-misconceptions-title.text: What is wrong with these four statements?

p11-misconceptions-ctx.name: p11-misconceptions-ctx
p11-misconceptions-ctx.text: Judge each one first, then read the correction on the right.

p11-misconceptions-m0-t.name: p11-misconceptions-m0-t
p11-misconceptions-m0-t.text: 'DenseNet has an unusually large number of layers.'

p11-misconceptions-c0-t.name: p11-misconceptions-c0-t
p11-misconceptions-c0-t.text: The point is many connections, and every layer is narrow.

p11-misconceptions-c1-t.name: p11-misconceptions-c1-t
p11-misconceptions-c1-t.text: Addition leaves channels unchanged, concatenation increases them.

p11-misconceptions-m2-t.name: p11-misconceptions-m2-t
p11-misconceptions-m2-t.text: 'Concatenation makes the channel count run away.'

p11-misconceptions-c2-t.name: p11-misconceptions-c2-t
p11-misconceptions-c2-t.text: The growth rate is small and transition layers compress.

p11-misconceptions-c3-t.name: p11-misconceptions-c3-t
p11-misconceptions-c3-t.text: ConvNeXt and others show CNNs are still competitive.

p12-quiz-ctx.name: p12-quiz-ctx
p12-quiz-ctx.text: The last two of the source's four questions (the first two belong to KP06); the source page marks no answers, so the answers and explanations are written from this unit ([Added]).

p12-quiz-q0-t.name: p12-quiz-q0-t
p12-quiz-q0-t.text:
Which statement about the wiring of DenseNet compared with ResNet is correct?
A. DenseNet still uses the addition of formula (11), only doubling the layers
B. DenseNet concatenates the outputs of earlier layers with formula (12); $l$ layers have about $l(l+1)/2$ connections
C. DenseNet deletes all skip connections
D. The growth rate $k$ must equal 1000

p12-quiz-a0-t.name: p12-quiz-a0-t
p12-quiz-a0-t.text: Answer B. DenseNet uses concatenation (formula 12), and l layers have l(l+1)/2 connections. A is ResNet's way; C is the opposite; the growth rate of D is usually small, e.g. 12.

p12-quiz-q1-t.name: p12-quiz-q1-t
p12-quiz-q1-t.text:
Which is correct about EfficientNet's compound scaling and the message of ConvNeXt?
A. EfficientNet scales depth, width and resolution together; ConvNeXt shows a modernized CNN can still compete with Transformers
B. EfficientNet only deepens and leaves width and resolution alone
C. ConvNeXt proves CNNs are completely obsolete
D. Both forbid convolutions

p12-quiz-a1-t.name: p12-quiz-a1-t
p12-quiz-a1-t.text: Answer A. Compound scaling enlarges all three together; ConvNeXt shows a modernized CNN can still compete. B (only deepening) is wrong; C and D are the opposite of the source.

p13-summary-title.name: p13-summary-title
p13-summary-title.text: One sentence, plain words, formulas: what to take away from KP07

p13-summary-ctx.name: p13-summary-ctx
p13-summary-ctx.text: Close the slides and try to say the one-sentence version yourself.

p13-summary-one-t.name: p13-summary-one-t
p13-summary-one-t.text: DenseNet connects every layer of a dense block to all later layers ($l$ layers have $l(l+1)/2$ weight matrices), uses concatenation (formula 12) instead of addition, and controls channels with a small growth rate $k$ and transition layers; EfficientNet scales depth, width and resolution together; ConvNeXt shows a modernized CNN can still compete with Transformers.

p13-summary-plain-t.name: p13-summary-plain-t
p13-summary-plain-t.text: ResNet is like each person only adding the previous person's notes after their own; DenseNet is like each person holding the notes of everyone before and writing one new page. Everyone's notes are in hand, no need to recopy, and each only writes one small page.

p13-summary-fix-h.name: p13-summary-fix-h
p13-summary-fix-h.text: Corrections and choices relative to the source

p13-summary-fix-t.name: p13-summary-fix-t
p13-summary-fix-t.text:
1. The way of counting l(l+1)/2 (including x0) is [Added].
2. The k0=16, k=12 example and 88→44 are illustrations.
3. The compound-scaling constants come from the original paper; the source gives none.

p13-summary-next-t.name: p13-summary-next-t
p13-summary-next-t.text: This finishes the classic CNN architectures of Week 7. Next week (Week 8) looks at applications of CNNs: image classification and object detection. In Weeks 12 and 13 we meet attention and the Transformer and compare it back with CNNs.

p01-hook-cue0.name: p01-hook-cue0
p01-hook-cue0.text: Recall first: ResNet's shortcut links only the input and output of one block, by addition.

p01-hook-cue1.name: p01-hook-cue1
p01-hook-cue1.text: DenseNet's way: in a dense block every layer connects to all later layers by concatenation.

p01-hook-cue2.name: p01-hook-cue2
p01-hook-cue2.text: The four questions of this unit, and finally a review of the whole Week 7.

p02-dense-nav.name: p02-dense-nav
p02-dense-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 02/13 · §1 DenseNet · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p02-dense-cue0.name: p02-dense-cue0
p02-dense-cue0.text: First the thick green lines: adjacent circles are linked, 4 connections, the wiring of a standard network.

p02-dense-cue1.name: p02-dense-cue1
p02-dense-cue1.text: Then the orange arcs: they jump over the circles in between and connect earlier outputs directly to later ones, 6 in all.

p02-dense-cue2.name: p02-dense-cue2
p02-dense-cue2.text: Every circle connects to all circles after it: 4+3+2+1=10, i.e. l(l+1)/2.

p02-dense-cue3.name: p02-dense-cue3
p02-dense-cue3.text: The larger l, the bigger the gap: l=6 is 21 versus 6, l=10 is 55 versus 10.

p02-dense-cue4.name: p02-dense-cue4
p02-dense-cue4.text: The point is not many layers but many connections.

p03-add-concat-nav.name: p03-add-concat-nav
p03-add-concat-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 03/13 · §2 Addition and concatenation · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p03-add-concat-cue0.name: p03-add-concat-cue0
p03-add-concat-cue0.text: ResNet uses addition (formula 11): equal shapes, and the channel count is unchanged after adding.

p03-add-concat-cue1.name: p03-add-concat-cue1
p03-add-concat-cue1.text: DenseNet uses concatenation (formula 12): all earlier outputs are joined along the channels.

p03-add-concat-cue2.name: p03-add-concat-cue2
p03-add-concat-cue2.text: Compare the channels: addition stays at 64; concatenation 16, 28, 40… ever more.

p03-add-concat-cue3.name: p03-add-concat-cue3
p03-add-concat-cue3.text: Additional: inside a dense block it is BN + 3×3 convolution + ReLU, and pooling sits in the transition layer between blocks.

p04-growth-nav.name: p04-growth-nav
p04-growth-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 04/13 · §3 Growth rate · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p04-growth-cue0.name: p04-growth-cue0
p04-growth-cue0.text: Layers 1 and 2: inputs of 16 and 28 maps; each layer produces only 12 maps itself, so it is narrow.

p04-growth-cue1.name: p04-growth-cue1
p04-growth-cue1.text: Each extra layer adds 12 maps to the input (newly produced by the previous layer): 40, 52.

p04-growth-cue2.name: p04-growth-cue2
p04-growth-cue2.text: By layer 6 the input is 76 maps.

p04-growth-cue3.name: p04-growth-cue3
p04-growth-cue3.text: At the end of the block there are 88 channels, k0+kL=16+6×12.

p04-growth-cue4.name: p04-growth-cue4
p04-growth-cue4.text: The six layers add up to 29,808 weights; the benefits are many shortcuts, good gradients and reusable features.

p05-practice-a-nav.name: p05-practice-a-nav
p05-practice-a-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 05/13 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p05-practice-a-cue0.name: p05-practice-a-cue0
p05-practice-a-cue0.text: Work it out yourself: connections for l=5, the input and end-of-block channels of layer 4, the weights of layer 3.

p05-practice-a-cue1.name: p05-practice-a-cue1
p05-practice-a-cue1.text: Answers: 15 versus 5; 60 maps and 96 channels; 4,320 weights.

p06-transition-nav.name: p06-transition-nav
p06-transition-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 06/13 · §3 Transition layer · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p06-transition-cue0.name: p06-transition-cue0
p06-transition-cue0.text: First step of the transition layer: batch normalization.

p06-transition-cue1.name: p06-transition-cue1
p06-transition-cue1.text: Second step: a 1×1 convolution compresses channels, e.g. 88 down to 44 (44 is an illustration, not the source's compression ratio).

p06-transition-cue2.name: p06-transition-cue2
p06-transition-cue2.text: Third step: 2×2 average pooling halves the side, 56 becomes 28.

p06-transition-cue3.name: p06-transition-cue3
p06-transition-cue3.text: The weights of the 1×1 convolution are 88×44=3,872.

p06-transition-cue4.name: p06-transition-cue4
p06-transition-cue4.text: Channels halved and side halved: the total drops to 1/8.

p06-transition-cue5.name: p06-transition-cue5
p06-transition-cue5.text: Finally average pooling and a fully connected layer with softmax; the channels are controlled by a small growth rate and transition layers.

p07-compound-nav.name: p07-compound-nav
p07-compound-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 07/13 · §4 EfficientNet and ConvNeXt · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p07-compound-cue0.name: p07-compound-cue0
p07-compound-cue0.text: Compound scaling: depth, width and resolution are multiplied by α^φ, β^φ, γ^φ, with αβ²γ²≈2.

p07-compound-cue1.name: p07-compound-cue1
p07-compound-cue1.text: The paper's constants α=1.2, β=1.1, γ=1.15: the product is 1.92, about 2.

p07-compound-cue2.name: p07-compound-cue2
p07-compound-cue2.text: φ=1: depth ×1.2, width ×1.1, resolution ×1.15, computation about ×1.92.

p07-compound-cue4.name: p07-compound-cue4
p07-compound-cue4.text: Another message: ConvNeXt shows a modernized CNN can still compete with Transformers.

p08-practice-b-nav.name: p08-practice-b-nav
p08-practice-b-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 08/13 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p08-practice-b-cue0.name: p08-practice-b-cue0
p08-practice-b-cue0.text: Work it out yourself: transition-layer weights and side, the multiples for φ=2, the difference between addition and concatenation.

p08-practice-b-cue1.name: p08-practice-b-cue1
p08-practice-b-cue1.text: Answers: 3,872 and 28; 1.44 / 1.21 / 1.3225 and 3.69; addition unchanged, concatenation increases.

p09-review-nav.name: p09-review-nav
p09-review-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 09/13 · §5 Week review · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p09-review-cue0.name: p09-review-cue0
p09-review-cue0.text: KP01–KP02: initialization first makes the network trainable; AlexNet wins big on ImageNet, leaving 'can it go deeper?'.

p09-review-cue1.name: p09-review-cue1
p09-review-cue1.text: KP03–KP04: VGG builds depth from small kernels, Inception controls computation with parallel paths and reduction.

p09-review-cue2.name: p09-review-cue2
p09-review-cue2.text: KP05–KP06: U-Net does per-pixel output; ResNet uses residuals to solve the degradation of too much depth.

p09-review-cue3.name: p09-review-cue3
p09-review-cue3.text: KP07: DenseNet concatenates to reuse features, then compound scaling and modernized CNNs; attention models are left.

p09-review-cue4.name: p09-review-cue4
p09-review-cue4.text: A note on reading the table: the weight counts have different settings and should not be compared directly.

p10-conclusion-nav.name: p10-conclusion-nav
p10-conclusion-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP07 · 10/13 · §5 Chapter conclusions · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p10-conclusion-cue0.name: p10-conclusion-cue0
p10-conclusion-cue0.text: First point: CNNs specialize in grid data; one layer is convolution → detector → pooling.

p10-conclusion-cue1.name: p10-conclusion-cue1
p10-conclusion-cue1.text: Second point: from LeNet and AlexNet to VGG, Inception, ResNet and DenseNet, each adds depth, efficiency and feature reuse.
